newsitem.title: GREECE: BANK/GREECE SELLS $60MLN,660MLN ECUS TO PROP UP DRS.
newsitem.headline: BANK/GREECE SELLS $60MLN,660MLN ECUS TO PROP UP DRS.

text.p: The Bank of Greece, the country's central bank, sold about $60 million and 660 million ecus for drachmas to support the national currency at today's fixing, dealers said.
"The central bank sold about $60 million and 660 million ecus to prop up the drachma," said a forex dealer at a foreign bank. "The intervention succeeded in pushing ecu/drachma below 310."
Ecu/drachma settled at 309.92 from 309.55 on Tuesday and mark/drachma at 156.990 from yesterday's 156.700, dealers said.
"No one expected London-based banks to buy such a large amount of ecus for drachams today. We were caught off guard," said a dealer. "It could relate to position squaring."
Dollar/drachma settled at 281.50 from 281.02 on Tuesday. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
